entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Mithridates V of Parthia (129–140 CE) was a Parthian contender who played a significant role in the kingdom's power struggles during the Late Parthian period.

As a key figure in the Parthian royal succession, Mithridates V's claim to the throne was contested by his relatives, including his son Vologases IV of Parthia, who eventually succeeded him.

Mithridates V's reign was marked by a series of military campaigns against the Roman Empire, which had been expanding its territories in the region.

Despite his efforts to resist Roman pressure, Mithridates V's kingdom ultimately succumbed to the Roman Empire's growing power, leading to the eventual incorporation of Parthia into the Roman Empire.

The legacy of Mithridates V can be seen in the continued influence of Parthian culture and traditions in the region, as well as the Roman Empire's own cultural and military strategies.

As the Roman historian Cassius Dio once said, 'The Parthians were a people of great courage and valour, and their empire was one of the greatest in the world.'

In the end, Mithridates V's story serves as a testament to the enduring power of human ambition and the complexities of regional politics in the ancient world.
